items.title: Finding the Volume of a Cube

sections.normalized_html: A room in the shape of a cube has an edge length of [MATH: 13] feet. What is the volume, in cubic feet, of the room?
sections.readable_text: A room in the shape of a cube has an edge length of [MATH: 13] feet. What is the volume, in cubic feet, of the room?

sections.normalized_html:
To find the volume of a cube, we use the formula [MATH: V = s^3,] where [MATH: s] is the edge length of the cube.

Here, the edge length is [MATH: 13] feet. Substituting into the formula, we get [MATH: V = 13^3.]

Now, we compute the cube: [MATH: 13^{3}|= 13 ⋅ 13 ⋅ 13; = 169 ⋅ 13; = 2,197]

Therefore, the volume of the cube is [MATH: 2{,}197] cubic feet.

items.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Cube

sections.normalized_html: A cube-shaped toy chest has one open face. Each edge of the chest measures [MATH: 30] centimeters. What is the exterior surface area, in square centimeters, of this open-front chest?
sections.readable_text: A cube-shaped toy chest has one open face. Each edge of the chest measures [MATH: 30] centimeters. What is the exterior surface area, in square centimeters, of this open-front chest?

sections.normalized_html:
The chest is shaped like a cube, meaning all its faces are squares of equal size. Since the front is open, it has only [MATH: 5] square faces: [MATH: 4] sides and [MATH: 1] back.

To find the total exterior surface area [MATH: S], we multiply the area of one square face by [MATH: 5.] So, [MATH: S = 5 \cdot s^2,] where [MATH: s] is the edge length of the cube.

Next, we substitute [MATH: s = 30,] and simplify: [MATH: S|= 5 ⋅ s^{2}; = 5 ⋅ 30^{2}; = 5 ⋅ 900; = 4,500]

Therefore, the surface area of the chest is [MATH: 4{,}500] square centimeters.

sections.normalized_html: A cube has a surface area of [MATH: 294] square centimeters. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the cube?
sections.readable_text: A cube has a surface area of [MATH: 294] square centimeters. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the cube?

sections.normalized_html:
We are given the cube's surface a. The formula for the surface area of a cube is [MATH: A = 6s^2,] where [MATH: s] is the side length.

We set up the equation and simplify: [MATH: 6s^{2}|= 294; s^{2}|= 49; s|= 7]

Now, we compute the volume using the formula [MATH: V = s^3{:}] [MATH: V|= 7^{3}; = 343]

So, the volume of the cube is [MATH: 343] cubic centimeters.
